full_judgment: 22. The learned Advocate for respondent Nos.1 and 2 cited only one decision, Saminada Pillai vs Subba Reddiar, ILR Madras Volume 1 (1876-78) 333, in support of his contention, which was not raised anywhere before, that his clients could not be joined in a suit for partition which had been brought about by amendment because they were alleged to be trespassers without any right and title. In that decision the facts were that in a suit for partition of the joint Inam lands of a Hindu Family, a number of cultivating ryots were joined as defendants whom the plaintiffs sought to eject. The ryots pleaded that the lands had been reclaimed by their forefathers, that they and their fathers had been in possession ever since, and that they had thereby acquired a permanent right of occupancy. They also pleaded that the suit was bad for multifariousness. It was held that the ryots were improperly joined as defendants in that suit. Evidently the principle applied in that case is not available in the facts of the present case, more so, because the respondents themselves in their written statement, inter alia, stated that "fractional share of the plaintiff as alleged by him cannot be declared without partition." The respondents claimed to have purchased 4½ decimals of land in the suit plot No. 243 from one Shahadat Mia and Morshed Miah on 10-5-1973. In this proceeding there is no question raised about misjoinder of parties and the respondents have been in the suit as defendants from before the two amendments that were made by the plaintiff in his plaint. The submission of Mr Zakir Hossain, learned Advocate, therefore, appears to be thoroughly misconceived.
